11 Blocks P, Q, R and S are made from material of the same density. Block T is made from a
material of twice the density of the material of the other blocks.
The cross-sectional area and height of each of the blocks are shown.

Which two blocks exert the same pressure on the ground?

hints: Start from pressure on the ground as weight over contact area, with weight $= mg$ and mass $=$ density $\times$ volume for blocks P, Q, R, S and T.
Write volume as cross-sectional area $A$ or $2A$ times height $h$ or $2h$, then see how the contact area cancels to leave pressure proportional to density $\times$ height.
List $\rho h$ for each block, remembering T uses $2\rho$ while the others use $\rho$, and look for two blocks with the same $2\rho h$ value.
walkthrough: Identify the givens from the diagram: P is $A, h$; Q is $2A, h$; R is $A, 2h$; S is $2A, 2h$; T is $A, h$. Let density of P, Q, R, S be $\rho$, so density of T is $2\rho$.
State the rule: pressure $p = F/A_{contact} = W/A_{contact}$. With $W = mg = \rho V g$ and $V = A_{contact}h$, this gives $p = \rho A_{contact} h g / A_{contact} = \rho h g$.

So pressure does not depend separately on contact area $A$ or $2A$; it depends only on density $\times$ height. Calculate $\rho \times$ height: P is $\rho h$, Q is $\rho h$, R is $\rho(2h) = 2\rho h$, S is $\rho(2h) = 2\rho h$.
For T, include double density: $p_T$ is proportional to $(2\rho)h = 2\rho h$. With $g$ common to all, compare values with units of pressure.
S and T both give $2\rho h g$ and all other pairings in the options mix $\rho h g$ with $2\rho h g$. This is option D.

A.explanation: P gives pressure proportional to $\rho h$ but T gives $2\rho h$ because T has twice the density, so T exerts twice the pressure of P.

B.explanation: Q has height $h$ and R has height $2h$ with the same density, so R exerts twice the pressure of Q.

C.explanation: Q has height $h$ and S has height $2h$ with the same density, so S exerts twice the pressure of Q.

D.explanation: S has $\rho \times 2h$ and T has $2\rho \times h$, both equal $2\rho h$, so pressures are equal.
